description.narrative:
The intervention has five objectives
1. To provide immediate allocation for medical treatments and devices
2. To provide mental health support to injured patients and their attendants
3. Special provisions for limp amputations prosthetics and rehabilitation services
4. To provide financial and livelihood support to families and individuals A new objective will be included as fifth objective according to the request 5. Evaluate and compare the readiness, response, and resilience of public and private healthcare facilities during mass casualty events, identifying systemic gaps and potential reforms.

Detta bidrag syftar till 1. Att ge omedelbar tilldelning för medicinska behandlingar och apparater 2. Att ge psykisk hälsostöd till skadade patienter och deras vårdare 3. Särskilda bestämmelser för amputationsproteser och rehabiliteringstjänster 4. Att ge ekonomiskt stöd och försörjningsstöd till familjer och individer

This contribution is aiming 1.To provide immediate allocation for medical treatments and devices 2.To provide mental health support to injured patients and their attendants 3.Special provisions for limp amputations prosthetics and rehabilitation services 4.To provide financial and livelihood support to families and individuals

The intervention contributed to a range of interrelated outcomes at individual, household, institutional, and system levels within a complex crisis context.
At the individual and household level, the intervention improved access to essential healthcare services and reduced financial vulnerability among severely injured individuals. A total of 260 beneficiaries received financial support amounting to approximately BDT 30.3 million, enabling continued access to surgery, medicines, rehabilitation, and postdischarge care. Follow up findings indicate that 42.5 per cent of transferred funds were utilized for core medical and recovery related expenditures, demonstrating that assistance was largely used in line with programe objectives. Beneficiaries reported reduced financial stress and improved capacity to manage their recovery, while reliance on negative coping mechanisms such as borrowing and asset sales decreased.
The intervention also supported early livelihood recovery and economic reintegration. Beneficiaries invested part of the support in income generating and resilience building activities, including livestock (30 per cent), savings (26 per cent), and small businesses (19 per cent). These investments contributed to increased self reliance, adaptation of livelihoods to post injury conditions, and improved household financial planning.
At the institutional level, the intervention strengthened transparent, equitable, and needs based targeting. A structured two stage scoring methodology enabled prioritization based on clinical severity and socioeconomic vulnerability across 669 identified cases, contributing to greater consistency and fairness in beneficiary selection. The intervention also strengthened implementing partners capacity in beneficiary verification, documentation, monitoring, and data driven decision making. Collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), hospital authorities, and other stakeholders further enhanced accountability and coordination.
At the systems level, the intervention generated broader positive effects beyond its immediate objectives. Advocacy efforts contributed to securing a tax exemption on humanitarian assistance, preserving approximately BDT 10 million for direct beneficiary support. Coordination with government institutions and complementary actors reduced duplication of assistance and enabled resources to be redirected towards unmet needs, particularly livelihood recovery.
The intervention further demonstrated the value of digital delivery mechanisms. The use of mobile financial services (bKash) enabled rapid, transparent, and traceable fund transfers, strengthening accountability, reducing transaction risks, and increasing beneficiary control over resources. Implementing organisations also strengthened their capacity to utilize digital financial systems for crisis response.
Finally, the intervention reinforced collaborative practices within both the health system and civil society. Health providers, community actors, and partner organisations continued to support injured individuals despite operational constraints, while the intervention helped formalize these efforts through structured coordination mechanisms.
Overall, the intervention demonstrates that targeted financial assistance, combined with transparent targeting, digital disbursement systems, and effective stakeholder coordination, can contribute to improved recovery outcomes, enhanced household resilience, strengthened institutional capacity, and broader systemic benefits.
